considered.reasoning: This is not deleveraging (which failed in this archive, α=0.6%) nor the level of rollover exposure, but a substitution between maturity buckets that leaves total debt unchanged, so it isolates maturity management as a distinct managerial and credit-access signal. It is the natural forward test of the archive's central finding — that the short-maturity bucket is what makes profits fragile — because it asks whether the market prices the act of removing that fragility rather than its static absence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashValidatedProfitVsClaims
considered.hypothesis: A firm should be credited only with the profitability that both its accrual accounts and its cash flow statement support, and such cash-validated earnings are most durable when the total claims eventually payable are small relative to the liquid resources already on hand.
considered.reasoning: The accrual-validation channel is entirely absent from the evaluated archive — every signal so far uses an accrual profitability leg — and the MIN operator implements it monotonically, demoting accrual-inflated firms to their cash profitability without the mid-distribution artifacts of an indicator. The conditioner expresses all claims per dollar of liquid assets, a claims-to-liquidity intensity that is distinct from the tested current-ratio and net-liquid-balance forms, so both legs contribute information the archive has not yet measured.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SelfFundedExpansionProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(re, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength appears when the firm's own retained profits, rather than an expanding stack of external claims, fund whatever the business needs; profitability accompanied by liabilities growing faster than retained earnings is being sustained by outside capital and will not persist once that capital tightens.
considered.reasoning: The critique of the earlier version was correct that Δcurrent assets loads on the accrual/asset-growth anomaly, so the resilience flow is re-expressed on the financing side only: retained-earnings formation net of total claim growth, which contains no working-capital accrual component. It differs from the failed Δdebt signal because it is a *mix* variable — a firm can grow liabilities and still score well if retained earnings grow faster — making it a test of self-funding rather than of deleveraging.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BankedProfitTrackRecord
considered.hypothesis: Pretax income measures profitability after every operating and financing cost the firm actually bears, and it is credible only when it has been repeatedly banked: a steadily rising stock of retained earnings relative to assets is the accumulated, audited record that reported profits were real and were kept inside the firm.
considered.reasoning: Both inputs are unused in the evaluated archive — pi has never been tested as a profitability leg and re has appeared only as a static ratio to liabilities (α=1.2%) — and the trend form converts retained earnings from a stale historical stock into a measure of current earnings persistence net of distributions. This tests the "persistent" limb of the economic story through the balance sheet rather than through funding structure, giving the batch a second mechanism that does not depend on near-term claim composition.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RisingConservatismProfit
considered.hypothesis: A profitable firm that raises its depreciation rate is shortening assumed asset lives and taking earnings down voluntarily — a costly, credible signal of conservative reporting — whereas a firm whose depreciation rate is falling is stretching asset lives to support reported profits that are not economically earned.
considered.reasoning: The level of depreciation intensity is confounded with industry technology, asset age, and goodwill-heavy denominators, but the year-on-year *change* within the same firm strips those out and isolates the discretionary accounting choice, which is the actual economic content of the conservatism hypothesis. It is therefore not a re-parameterization of the gen-4 winner but the within-firm identification of the mechanism the winner is claimed to capture.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitFloorConservatism
considered.hypothesis: Conservative depreciation matters most when the profitability it depresses is a floor rather than a peak: a firm whose *worst* return on assets in three years is high, achieved while charging aggressive depreciation, has demonstrably durable operating strength rather than a favorable single year.
considered.reasoning: The persistence limb of the economic story has never been properly tested in this archive — three-year averages appeared only alongside failed volatility conditioners, and the five-year minimum used in gen 0 collapsed coverage to 0.09 — so a three-year floor paired with the strongest conditioner tests whether durability adds to the conservatism effect at acceptable coverage cost. If the FMB t-statistic exceeds the 5.09 benchmark, downside profitability is the better profitability construct and should anchor the final generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LeanFixedBaseProfit
considered.hypothesis: Profits earned on a small base of illiquid, long-lived capital reflect a business model that does not need to sink cash into replaceable hard assets to compete, so the earnings are both defensible and cheap to sustain; the same profits earned on a heavy fixed base are hostage to maintenance capital spending and to the write-down risk in that base.
considered.reasoning: This is the competing-hypothesis test the gen-4 result actually needs: dp/(at−act) is high both when a firm depreciates conservatively and simply when its net long-term asset base is small relative to operations, and turnover on long-term capital isolates the second reading using no income-statement item, so it cannot inherit any mechanical link with the profitability leg. If it predicts as strongly as the depreciation conditioner, the channel is capital-light operating structure rather than accounting conservatism, which changes what we should refine in the final generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FundsValidatedProfitVsClaims
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oibdp, COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(lt, act))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm should be credited only with the lesser of its accrual cash profit and the cash its operations actually generated, and such validated earnings are most durable when total claims are small relative to liquid resources already on hand.
considered.reasoning: This keeps the cash-validation operator intact — the critique correctly noted that the previous revision discarded it — and repairs coverage instead at its true source, the availability of the cash-flow statement, by falling back to funds from operations (net income plus depreciation), the standard pre-SFAS-95 cash proxy and an economically justified missing-data convention rather than a blanket patch. If alpha holds near the 4.2% of the restricted-sample parent while coverage rises toward the archive norm, the cash-validation channel is real and not a sample artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EarnedEquityProfit
considered.hypothesis: The share of book equity that was earned and retained rather than contributed by investors is a lifecycle marker of proven profitability: firms whose capital base is self-generated have demonstrated repeatable earnings, while equally profitable firms whose equity is mostly paid-in are earlier-stage or post-deficit and their current returns are far less likely to persist.
considered.reasoning: This replaces a rediscovery of the working-capital accrual anomaly with a channel the archive has barely touched — the only retained-earnings test scaled re by liabilities, which measures solvency, whereas scaling by book equity measures the earned-versus-contributed composition of capital and is close to orthogonal to leverage and liquidity. The interaction claim is specific: current profitability should be much more persistent, and hence more underpriced, in firms whose entire equity base is the accumulated record of past profits.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AgeAdjustedProfitConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(at, TS_SUM(dp, 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Book assets are reported net of accumulated depreciation, so an old asset base inflates measured return on assets; if the depreciation-intensity interaction is genuine conservatism rather than an age artifact, it must survive when profitability is measured against an approximate gross asset base that restores what has already been written off.
considered.reasoning: The previous version changed both legs at once and therefore identified nothing; here the conditioner is held byte-identical to the gen-4 winner and only the profitability denominator is de-biased, so the comparison is controlled and interpretable. A materially weaker result would say the archive's strongest signal is largely a stale-book-value effect, while a preserved result would justify making conservatism the anchor channel for the remaining generations — and the five-year depreciation accumulation is the only gross-asset proxy constructible from the permitted variable set.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashValidatedConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oiadp, SUB(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), dp)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
considered.hypothesis: The most durable earnings are those that clear two independent audits at once — the cash flow statement confirms them, and they were reported under a conservative depreciation policy that already charged the asset base heavily — so the firm's operating strength is understated on both the accrual and the capital-consumption dimension.
considered.reasoning: These are the archive's two best-identified channels and they are economically independent (one is a cash-versus-accrual test, the other an asset-charging policy test), so their combination is a genuine test of complementarity rather than a stack of correlated funding ranks. The cash leg is expressed on the same after-depreciation basis as the conditioner's parent (OCF less depreciation versus EBIT), preserving the negative mechanical link that made the gen-4 result conservative rather than mechanical, and the funds-from-operations fallback keeps coverage at the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LongClaimsPerLiquidDollar
considered.hypothesis: If what makes profitable firms fragile is the size of claims relative to the liquid resources available to meet them, then long-term debt per liquid dollar should predict returns much like short-term debt does; if instead callability is the mechanism, long-maturity claims should be largely harmless because no creditor can demand repayment in the relevant horizon.
considered.reasoning: This is the one cell of the maturity-versus-liquidity decomposition the archive has never run: dlc/act, dlc/lt, lt/act and lt/at have all been tested but dltt against the liquid base has not, and the two hypotheses make opposite predictions about it. The answer determines what the final signal should condition on — total claim burden or specifically callable claims — and it carries no coverage cost.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: HistoricLowLeverageProfit
considered.hypothesis: Financial health is partly firm-specific: a profitable company sitting at the lowest leverage of its own recent history has completed a balance-sheet repair and has maximum capacity to absorb shocks, regardless of whether its leverage looks high or low relative to other firms.
considered.reasoning: Every leverage conditioner tested so far is cross-sectional, and the two dynamic ones used a single-year change; a within-firm position measure is a distinct object that nets out the permanent industry and business-model component of leverage that cross-sectional ranks cannot remove. It is the only genuinely untested quality construction remaining in the permitted variable set, and its coverage cost from the five-year window should be read against the 0.09–0.10 archive precedent.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FundsValidatedRolloverProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oibdp, COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-validated operating profitability and freedom from callable near-term debt are separate defences against profit reversal — one against accounting overstatement, the other against forced retrenchment — and firms possessing both should command the largest premium.
considered.reasoning: The archive's two highest alphas (4.2% each) come from these ingredients used separately with different partners, and their parents have distinctly different risk profiles (Sharpe 0.19 versus 0.25), which suggests imperfect correlation and therefore scope for genuine reinforcement rather than redundancy. As a consolidation cell this is directly actionable: if alpha rises materially above 4.2% with a t-statistic above 4, the final recommended signal should pair cash validation with maturity risk rather than choose between them.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OperatingCycleStabilityProfit
considered.hypothesis: A profitable firm whose operating cycle is stable — receivables and inventory holding a constant relation to sales year after year — has predictable demand, disciplined credit terms, and no need for emergency financing, whereas a swinging cycle reveals demand shocks or channel stuffing that make current profitability unreliable.
considered.reasoning: The archive has tested stability only on financing variables (leverage volatility failed, short-term-debt volatility worked at α = 3.1%, t = 2.8), never on the operating side, so this asks whether the stability limb of the economic story runs through operations rather than through funding. It also replaces a measurement-noise tweak with a distinct economic quantity: the variability of working-capital intensity is close to orthogonal to the level effects already documented, and it uses only universally reported items so coverage should hold near the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MaintenanceFundedProfit
considered.hypothesis: The committed cash obligation that a profitable firm cannot escape is the replacement of the capital it consumes each year, so liquid assets measured in years of depreciation charge is the true endurance ratio: firms that could fund many years of capital maintenance from resources already on hand never have to cut investment or refinance to keep their profit engine intact.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the archive's clearest null, LiquidityRunwayProfit (fmb t = 0.31), whose committed-cost denominator combined SG&A and interest — items that are frequently missing, often embedded in COGS, and near zero for asset-heavy firms — with depreciation, the one committed reinvestment flow reported by essentially every firm and the one that maps directly to the asset base being consumed. It also functions as a sharp counterweight test for the conservatism channel: dp appears here in the denominator, so if high-depreciation firms still score well through their liquid buffer, the two mechanisms are separable rather than two readings of the same variable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: QualityIndexProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires quality on two economically independent dimensions — earnings reported under a conservative capital-charging policy, and an absence of callable claims against liquid resources — so profitability should be conditioned on a two-dimensional quality index rather than on either dimension alone.
considered.reasoning: This is the consolidation the evidence now supports: the two conditioners come from different data domains (income-statement accounting policy versus balance-sheet maturity structure) and have complementary statistical profiles, one carrying the slope and Sharpe, the other the alpha. Using SUMRANK to build the index preserves cross-sectional dispersion — the specific defect that made earlier three-way rank *products* shrink the spread — so this tests complementarity without the compression that doomed the gen-2 triple screen.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IntangibleProfitConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Adding back expensed R&D restores true operating profitability, and pairing that restored measure with a conservative depreciation policy identifies firms whose economic earnings exceed reported earnings on both the intangible and the tangible dimension.
considered.reasoning: This is one of the two untested cells of the profitability-leg × conditioner factorial that must be filled before a final recommendation, and it is not a foregone conclusion: R&D-intensive firms typically report *low* depreciation rates, so the two legs select partly opposing populations and the interaction could easily be weaker than either parent. Whichever way it resolves, it tells us whether the final signal should use restored or reported profitability alongside the conservatism conditioner.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IntangibleProfitRollover
considered.hypothesis: R&D-restored profitability is the most complete measure of operating strength, and it is most durable in firms with no callable debt, because rollover pressure forces exactly the discretionary investment cuts that destroy an intangible-based competitive position.
considered.reasoning: This is the second missing factorial cell and pairs the archive's highest-alpha profitability leg (4.1%, ls_talpha 4.07 with a liquidity conditioner) with its highest-alpha conditioner (4.2%, t 3.79 with plain ROA), so it is the single most likely candidate to exceed the 4.2% alpha ceiling that every construction has hit so far. Evaluated alongside Signal 4 it also separates whether the R&D add-back interacts with funding safety or with accounting conservatism, which the two parents cannot distinguish.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FragileEarningsRollover
considered.hypothesis: Callable debt is dangerous precisely when operating results are unpredictable: a firm with steady returns can always refinance, and a firm with volatile returns can survive a bad year if nothing is due, but the combination of earnings instability and maturing claims is what forces distressed retrenchment and destroys profitability.
considered.reasoning: Every archive signal conditions the *level* of profitability, never its stability, on funding structure, yet the economic story's "stable" limb predicts an interaction specifically between second-moment earnings risk and callable claims — a joint-fragility mechanism rather than two additive quality screens. It is also a useful diagnostic for the final generations: if it performs comparably to level-based pairings, the premium is compensation for distress-state risk, whereas if it fails, the level of operating strength is what the market misprices.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DualChargeConservatismProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Conservative reporting depresses earnings through two independent charges — fast write-down of tangible capital and outright expensing of intangible investment — and a firm that remains highly profitable while making both charges has the most deeply understated operating strength.
considered.reasoning: The critique of the raw sum was correct: adding R&D dollars to depreciation over a small long-term-asset base lets an R&D/PPE explosion dominate, so each charge is now measured as a rate on an appropriate base and combined through SUMRANK, which ranks the two components separately and is immune to their scale difference. This also distinguishes the proposal from the published R&D-intensity effect, because a firm scores highly only by being conservative on *both* dimensions, and the archive has never tested R&D intensity as a conditioner — only as an add-back inside the profitability leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MaturityMismatchProfit
considered.hypothesis: The classic financing error is funding long-lived, illiquid assets with debt that must be renegotiated every year; profitability generated on a fixed asset base carrying heavy short-maturity funding is hostage to the credit cycle, whereas the same profitability with maturity-matched funding is durable.
considered.reasoning: This replaces a near-collinear reparameterization with a genuinely different object: dlc/act asks whether liquid resources cover maturing claims, while dlc/(at−act) asks whether the *illiquid* asset base is being financed at the wrong maturity, and the two denominators are drawn from disjoint parts of the balance sheet so the measures are far from collinear. It also completes the maturity-structure map alongside the already-tested dlc/lt and the now-rejected dltt/act, telling us whether the callability premium reflects a coverage shortfall or an asset-liability duration mismatch.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalizedRnDProfitRollover
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
considered.hypothesis: If expensed R&D is genuinely investment, it belongs on both sides of the profitability ratio: the income statement understates earnings by the current year's spend and the balance sheet understates capital by the accumulated knowledge stock, so a fully capitalized return on assets is the correct measure of durable operating strength.
considered.reasoning: The archive's highest-alpha signal adds R&D back only to the numerator, which mechanically inflates measured returns for research-intensive firms and leaves open whether the premium reflects true productivity or a denominator omission — capitalizing the five-year knowledge stock removes that asymmetry. This is a substantive measurement correction rather than a recombination, and it is the cleanest available test of why the R&D-restored leg outperforms; its coverage cost from the five-year accumulation should be read against the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StableEarningsConservatism
considered.hypothesis: Conservative capital charging is most informative for firms whose operating returns are steady: a stable earnings stream reported under aggressive depreciation is understated economic income that will keep repeating, whereas volatile earnings tell us little about the policy's meaning.
considered.reasoning: The second-moment channel proved real when paired with callable debt (α 2.9%, t 3.0), and this fills the remaining cell of the {level, stability} × {conservatism, callability} design, pairing earnings stability with the archive's most powerful conditioner. It also serves as a discriminating test of the mispricing story: if stability substitutes for the profitability level without loss, the premium is about predictability of understated earnings rather than about the level of operating strength.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxValidatedProfitRollover
considered.hypothesis: Tax expense is the one earnings validation a firm pays real money for: profits that generate a large tax charge relative to assets have been asserted to the tax authority as well as to investors, so they are far harder to manufacture than accrual profits, and such validated earnings are durable when no callable debt threatens the business.
considered.reasoning: Cash-flow validation was tested twice and added nothing beyond the underlying profitability (α fell from 4.2% to 3.8% when paired with the rollover conditioner), so the natural next validation channel is the book-tax dimension, which no archive signal has touched and which is orthogonal to the operating-cash-flow test because it screens for non-recurring, non-taxable, and accounting-only income. Pretax income and bottom-line income are both universally reported, so this carries no coverage cost and gives the profitability leg a genuinely different economic definition rather than a re-scaling.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ReserveConservatismProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lt, dltt), lct), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Liabilities that are neither long-term debt nor current obligations are largely deferred taxes, pension and warranty reserves, and other provisions — balance-sheet conservatism in recognizing future costs early — so a highly profitable firm carrying large reserves has understated both its earnings and its equity and is reporting from a position of strength.
considered.reasoning: This moves the conservatism mechanism, which the archive has established only on the income statement through depreciation policy, to the liability side of the balance sheet where it has never been measured, and the residual-liability construction uses only quality-exclusive items so it cannot be a restatement of any tested leverage or liquidity ratio. It is also economically linked to the depreciation finding in a testable way — accelerated tax depreciation is the main source of deferred tax liabilities — so a positive result would corroborate the conservatism interpretation from an independent data domain.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FloorRestoredProfitConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
considered.hypothesis: The profitability that earns a quality premium is the level sustained in the worst of the last three years; a three-year floor on intangible-restored returns, reported under conservative depreciation, identifies operating strength that has already been tested by a downturn.
considered.reasoning: The critique is accepted: this now varies exactly one element — TS_MIN — against the standing archive baseline IntangibleProfitConservatism (fmb 6.19, α 3.9%, t 3.51), holding the conditioner and the profitability definition fixed, so any change in alpha or slope is attributable to the floor construction alone. That attribution matters for the final generation because the floor previously raised the slope but cost alpha when applied to plain ROA, and we need to know whether it does the same to the restored leg before choosing the final form.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PolicyRateConservatismProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(dp, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Depreciation divided by *net* long-term assets rises mechanically as an asset base ages, conflating a firm's useful-life policy with the vintage of its equipment; measured against an estimated *gross* base it isolates the deliberate policy choice, which is the conservatism the hypothesis is actually about.
considered.reasoning: This is the measurement correction the critic has flagged since gen 4 — asset-age contamination of dp/(at−act) — and gen 5 only de-biased the profitability denominator, never the conditioner itself, so the question remains open and is central to interpreting the archive's strongest channel. If the policy rate performs as well or better, the finding is genuinely about conservative reporting and generalizes; if it degrades materially, the premium is an asset-age/stale-book-value effect and the final signal should say so rather than claim conservatism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AmortizedRnDProfitRollover
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
considered.hypothesis: If R&D is capitalized it must also be amortized: economic operating profit equals reported EBIT plus the current year's R&D spend less the periodic write-off of the accumulated knowledge stock, measured against an asset base that includes that stock, and this properly specified return is what should interact with freedom from callable debt.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the internal inconsistency the critic identified in CapitalizedRnDProfitRollover, which added back the full current spend while charging no amortization against the capitalized stock, thereby flattering steady-state R&D spenders; the five-year moving average of R&D is exactly the straight-line amortization of a five-year knowledge stock, so the numerator and denominator are now consistent. Since that half-specified version already reached α 4.7% (t 4.22), the corrected version isolates whether the intangible premium reflects genuine productivity net of intangible capital consumption.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxValidatedConservatism
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(pi, ib), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(dp, 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Two independent hard validations of earnings coincide here: a large tax charge proves profits were asserted to the tax authority, and a conservative book depreciation policy proves they were reported after a heavy capital charge, so firms scoring on both have operating strength that neither accounting discretion nor selective disclosure could manufacture.
considered.reasoning: The tax channel is new to the archive and worked modestly with the funding conditioner (α 2.6%, t 2.4), but it should interact far more informatively with conservatism, since heavy book depreciation ordinarily *reduces* taxable-income conformity — a firm that charges book depreciation aggressively and still pays substantial tax is unusually credible. This is the only cell that pairs two validation mechanisms rather than a validation with a balance-sheet risk measure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CredibleDepreciationPolicyProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: A depreciation rate that stays constant year after year reflects a stable, non-discretionary useful-life policy, whereas a rate that jumps around signals write-off timing, impairment management, or acquisition-driven restatement of the asset base — so profitability reported under a *credible* policy is more trustworthy than profitability reported under a shifting one.
considered.reasoning: Every conservatism test so far has been about the level or the direction of the depreciation rate; its stability is a different economic object — reporting credibility rather than reporting conservatism — and it directly addresses the measurement-noise concern the critic raised about capex timing and acquisitions contaminating the level. As the exploratory slot it is also diagnostic for interpretation: if credibility predicts independently of level, the channel is about the trustworthiness of reported earnings rather than about understatement per se.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FreeOperatingProfitRollover
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oiadp, dp), DELTA(SUB(at, act), 1)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
considered.hypothesis: The profit an owner can actually withdraw is cash operating income less the net investment required to keep the long-lived asset base intact, so EBITDA minus the change in net long-term assets is the true distributable operating return; such genuinely free profitability is durable when no callable debt has a prior claim on the firm's liquid resources.
considered.reasoning: This replaces an index recombination with a new profitability construct that unifies the archive's two accounting findings economically rather than statistically — firms scoring highly are exactly those that charge heavy depreciation while not having to spend it back, which is what the conservatism channel has been capturing indirectly through dp/(at−act). Pairing it with the highest-alpha conditioner keeps the funding channel intact without SUMRANK dilution, and every input is universally reported so coverage should match the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrossInvestedCapitalProfitRollover
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(at, TS_SUM(dp, 5)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
considered.hypothesis: Total invested capital is reported assets plus what accounting has removed from them — accumulated depreciation on tangible assets and the entire expensed intangible stock — so return on gross invested capital is the only profitability measure comparable across firms of different asset age and different intangible intensity, and it is durable when callable claims are absent.
considered.reasoning: The critique was correct that the previous denominator restored only the intangible omission, never accumulated depreciation, so the "consistent invested capital" claim was not what the expression computed; both write-backs are now applied, making the measure internally coherent for the first time in the archive. Pairing it with the callable-debt conditioner rather than with the depreciation conditioner also removes the mechanical entanglement between a depreciation-adjusted denominator and a depreciation-rate conditioner, so the test cleanly asks whether true capital productivity, not accounting artifact, drives the interaction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StressStateProfitFunding
considered.hypothesis: A firm's durability should be judged in its bad state, not its average one: the lowest restored return it earned in three years paired with the highest short-term-debt exposure it carried over the same window describes how the business looks when operations and funding are simultaneously at their worst.
considered.reasoning: This is not a single-component swap but a change in the evaluation state — both legs are moved from their central tendency to their adverse extreme, testing the risk-based reading of the entire archive, namely that the premium compensates for how bad the joint profitability-and-funding state can get rather than for average characteristics. The two ingredients performed well individually with conventional partners (floor profitability fmb 6.30, Sharpe 0.461; peak rollover exposure α 3.4%), yet their worst-state pairing has never been run, and it is the cleanest available discrimination between distress-risk compensation and mispricing of understated earnings.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: Mean-ROA-scaled-by-ROA-volatility is essentially the standard "earnings stability" leg of published quality/QMJ and earnings-volatility anomalies rather than a new interaction, and dividing by a five-year volatility that can be near zero makes the cross-sectional ranking hostage to a handful of denominator outliers that 1% winsorization only partly tames.

This is a mechanical crossing of two canonical anomalies (profitability and Sloan accruals), and the hard indicator is internally incoherent because zeroing the industry rank places accrual-inflated firms at the middle of the signal distribution — above genuinely low-ROA but cash-confirmed firms — so the sort no longer tests the stated conditional hypothesis.

The expression is a plain additive rank sum of profitability and negative leverage — two heavily documented, already-priced characteristics — and it does not implement the stated "unlevered profitability" concept at all, since no unlevering or conditioning actually occurs.

Scaling current EBITDA/assets by a five-year count of profitable years is a coherent profitability-times-track-record interaction with a defensible extrapolation mechanism, though it overlaps materially with Piotroski-style persistence screens and creates an awkward discontinuity where loss-making firms with zero profitable years collapse to exactly zero rather than to the bottom of the sort.

The expected sign is backwards on the second leg: a rising net-working-capital-to-assets trend is mechanically growth in working-capital accruals, which the accrual and net-operating-asset literature shows predicts *lower* future returns, so the composite pits gross profitability against a component with a documented opposite-sign loading.

Using the five-year minimum ROA as a downside "profitability floor" alongside cash-flow coverage of liabilities is a defensible and reasonably distinct construction, but it remains an additive rank composite of two quality/distress measures and min-ROA will be highly collinear with mean ROA, so the incremental content over a standard profitability sort needs to be demonstrated.

Both legs are essentially profitability scaled by a balance-sheet stock (oiadp/at and oibdp/lt are highly correlated), so the "bottleneck" MIN is a cosmetic operator swap on the archive's already-tested SelfFinancedProfitPower/TroughProfitSolvency rank-composite of profitability and profit-to-liability coverage rather than a genuine new interaction.

EBITDA-less-interest over total liabilities is a textbook debt-service-coverage/credit-quality metric (an Ohlson/Piotroski-style ingredient), and since xint is small relative to oibdp the measure is dominated by oibdp/lt, making it a single-ratio profitability-scaled-by-liabilities sort very close to the archive's oancf/lt leg rather than a cross-theme interaction.

The working-capital-intensity leg is close to the known net-operating-assets/accruals anomaly, but the sign orientation is correct and consistent with that literature, and conditioning profitability on operating-cycle cash intensity is a coherent, non-trivial interaction — the main risks are sale-in-denominator instability for low-revenue firms and coverage loss from act/lct.

The Δleverage leg is close to the documented debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly, so part of the return is likely already spanned, but the expected sign is internally consistent and interacting financing direction with profitability is a legitimate and reasonably distinct test of "self-funded" operating strength.

Financing-policy stability is a plausibly less-mined channel than earnings stability and the expression matches the hypothesis, but a standard deviation estimated from three annual leverage observations is extremely noisy and will largely proxy for asset growth/issuance activity, so the effective information content may be thin.

The effective-interest term xint/lt has an order-of-magnitude smaller cross-sectional dispersion than oiadp/at (and is downward-biased and noisy because lt includes non-interest-bearing liabilities), so the spread will correlate near-unity with a plain ROA sort — a rediscovery of the profitability anomaly dressed as a cost-of-capital spread.

This is a mechanical stacking of the two best archive signals' conditioners onto the same profitability leg rather than a new mechanism, and multiplying three highly correlated funding-pressure ranks will mostly shrink cross-sectional dispersion and coverage without testing anything the parents' correlation could not reveal directly.

The decomposition logic is stated correctly (the NEG((act−lct)/sale) long leg does load on high current liabilities, so isolating lct/at is a coherent attribution test), though the resulting conditioner is close to a plain leverage-level screen of the type that has already repeatedly failed in this archive.

Replacing a static coverage stock with liquid assets scaled by a committed cost flow is a genuinely different economic construct (cost-structure endurance rather than accounting liquidity) and the expression matches the hypothesis, with the main caveats being xsga availability and near-zero denominators for low-overhead firms, both partly mitigated by industry ranking.

Stripping the liquid-asset denominator out of the archive's strongest conditioner cleanly separates maturity concentration from liquidity, the sign is correct and zero-debt handling is sensible, with the only reservation that short-term-debt-share return predictability is itself a semi-established credit-risk finding so the incremental novelty rests on the interaction with profitability.

By the proposal's own admission this holds economic content fixed and changes only the aggregation operator, which is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and MIN of two ranks discards the upper-tail information that gives the rank product its dispersion.

A legitimate and cleanly specified attribution test that isolates whether the archive winner's alpha comes from the R&D add-back or the liquidity leg, but the low prior on yet another leverage-level conditioner (and its near-duplication of LowNearTermClaimsProfit's economic content) limits its standalone value.

This is a mechanical crossing of two already-tested archive legs (the xrd add-back profitability of IntangibleProfitLowLeverage/WithSlack and the dlc/act conditioner of RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit) that will almost certainly "work" by construction while testing no new economic claim — the stated super-additivity story (R&D is cut first under rollover pressure) is not identified by a simple rank product.

The rationale is internally inconsistent — revt−cogs−xsga differs from the already-tested oiadp only by depreciation (it is essentially oibdp, also already used in the archive), so it does not remove accruals or special items as claimed and is ~0.9+ correlated with the existing profitability leg, making this a cosmetic variant of RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit built on a published (Novy-Marx) profitability measure.

Isolating the non-debt residual of current liabilities scaled as payables-days is a genuinely untested cell and reconciles the WorkingCapitalLightProfit sign puzzle, but the expected sign is contestable — the net-operating-asset/accrual literature and trade-credit bargaining-power evidence both imply high payables should predict *higher* returns, so the NEG() direction may be backwards.

Change in short-term debt is close to a catalogued anomaly (the net-external-financing / change-in-current-debt family), so novelty is limited, but the specific question — whether the *change* in the fragile maturity bucket adds to the level effect after Δtotal-debt failed — is a coherent and cheaply diagnostic follow-up.

Relocating the stability concept from a leverage variable that carries no alpha to the one funding variable that does is a defensible substantive change, but a 3-observation volatility of dlc/act is mechanically increasing in its level, so any positive result risks being a noisy proxy for the already-established level effect rather than evidence for funding stability per se.

Replacing the stock-of-liquid-assets conditioner with a flow-coverage measure is the most economically distinct proposal in this batch and addresses a real gap (asset-light firms with thin balance sheets but ample cash generation), though the reviewer should note that both legs embed operating income, so the signal partly compounds profitability with an inverse-leverage tilt and the denominator becomes unstable for near-debt-free firms.

This is the archived PayableStretchProfit with the conditioner's rank orientation reversed and the expected sign flipped to match its realized negative alpha — a mechanical in-sample sign fit on an already-evaluated construction rather than a new hypothesis test.

(lct−dlc)/lct is just 1 − dlc/lct, a denominator swap on the already-tested ShortDebtShareProfit (NEG dlc/lt, α=3.4%, t=3.5) and highly collinear with it, so the "mix vs. level" framing does not make this substantively different from an archived winner.

This is the only proposal opening a genuinely untested channel (accounting conservatism rather than funding structure) with a coherent mechanism and full coverage, though the reviewer should be aware that dp/(at−act) is heavily contaminated by asset age, goodwill/intangible-heavy denominators, and is partly a mechanical restatement of EBITDA-based profitability.

(act−dlc)/lct decomposes into act/lct minus dlc/lct, both of which are already-tested conditioners in the archive (IntangibleProfitWithSlack, RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, SurvivalHorizonProfit uses the identical act−dlc numerator), so this is a recombination of known ingredients rather than a new economic channel.

The Δact/at leg rewards firms accumulating current assets, which is the long leg of the well-documented working-capital accruals/asset-growth anomaly and predicts *low* returns, so the stated positive expected sign is in tension with the expression's dominant known component; the Δdlc leg meanwhile duplicates ShrinkingRolloverExposure.

The conditioner is byte-identical to the archive's best performer (RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, NEG dlc/act) and only the profitability denominator changes, making this a one-input tweak of an evaluated signal, with the added hazard that at−act goes to zero for asset-light firms and produces unstable, outlier-driven ratios.

The stated logic is backwards — since oibdp = oiadp + dp, replacing EBIT with EBITDA *introduces* a mechanical positive link between the two legs (dp raises both) rather than breaking it, so a positive result would be uninformative about the conservatism-versus-cash-earnings question the test claims to settle.

The within-firm change in depreciation intensity is a coherent, economically motivated identification of the discretionary-conservatism mechanism (essentially the Beneish DEPI logic, but as an interaction with profitability rather than a standalone manipulation flag), and the sign convention matches the expression; the main risk is noise from capex timing and acquisitions in the denominator.

The coverage-repair motivation is legitimate, but EBITDA − Δ(act−lct) is not "the same economic quantity" as MIN(EBITDA, OCF) — it drops the cash-validation/conservatism operator entirely and, because act includes cash and lct includes dlc, it penalizes cash accumulation and short-term debt paydown, contaminating the accrual adjustment it is meant to make.

A defensible but low-information refinement: TS_MIN(ROA,3) is highly correlated with contemporaneous ROA so the test is close to a reparameterization of the gen-4 winner, and the claim that the persistence limb is untested overstates matters given MA(ROA,3) and TS_MIN(ROA,5) both already appear in the archive.

The negative-change-in-net-working-capital leg is a direct restatement of Sloan's working-capital accrual anomaly (and its profitability interaction is the standard earnings-quality/quality-minus-junk construction), so this is rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme mechanism, and using act−lct rather than non-cash/non-debt working capital adds measurement contamination.

The gross-asset denominator is a reasonable idea in principle, but the design does not do what the rationale claims — it changes both the profitability denominator and the conditioner relative to the gen-4 result, so it cannot identify whether that result is an asset-age artifact, and TS_SUM(dp,5) added to total assets is a crude, monotone-ish adjustment likely to leave the industry-rank leg nearly unchanged.

A defensible composite of the archive's two strongest independent channels, but the double-subtraction of `dp` (once inside the cash leg's `oancf - dp`, once implicitly rewarded in the `dp/(at-act)` conditioner) creates an offsetting mechanical link that will partly cancel rather than reinforce the two effects, so the "complementarity" claim is weaker than stated.

This is a cosmetic smoothing variant of ConservativeDepreciationProfit (already at fmb_tstat 5.09, ls_talpha 3.30) with no new economic content — a three-year moving average of the same conditioner is exactly the kind of measurement tweak the objective asks researchers not to substitute for a substantive improvement.

The conditioner is identical to the already-tested RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit and the only change is subtracting `dp` a second time from an income measure that is already after depreciation — an arbitrary, uncalibrated stress charge that mostly re-ranks firms by capital intensity rather than by accounting conservatism, so it neither cleanly "internalizes" the gen-4 channel nor constitutes a distinct hypothesis.

A legitimate and cheap decomposition test of an untested cell (dltt/act) that discriminates between the callability and total-claim-burden mechanisms, though it is largely a component of the already-tested lt/act conditioner and the framing admits a null result is the informative outcome, which caps its standalone value.

A within-firm time-series position measure of leverage is a genuinely distinct object from every cross-sectional or one-year-change conditioner in the archive and plausibly nets out permanent business-model leverage, though the claim that it is the "only" untested construction is overstated and the five-year window's coverage cost needs watching.

A reasonable consolidation of the two highest-alpha ingredients, but dlc/act and the previously paired lt/act are components of the same liquidity-versus-claims construct, so the assumed imperfect correlation is optimistic and the likely outcome is a marginal rather than reinforcing gain.

A defensible additive-index merge of the archive's two strongest conditioners (depreciation conservatism and rollover exposure) that plausibly avoids rank-product compression, but it is an incremental recombination of already-tested components whose likely outcome is an interpolation between the two parents rather than a new mechanism.

The numerator mixes a genuine depreciation *rate* with an R&D *intensity* term over a long-term-asset denominator that is tiny for exactly the asset-light R&D firms the add-back targets, so the conditioner will be dominated by an R&D/PPE explosion — effectively rediscovering the published R&D-intensity anomaly already probed by IntangibleProfitWithSlack/IntangibleProfitLowLeverage rather than generalizing conservatism.

Since act typically dwarfs oibdp for the vast majority of firms, dlc/(act+oibdp) will be near-collinear with the already-tested dlc/act in RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit, making this a cosmetic reparameterization rather than the substantive redefinition of "resources" the reasoning claims.

A legitimate factorial cell whose value is diagnostic rather than exploratory — the two legs are known to select partly opposing populations, so the test genuinely resolves whether the final construction should use restored or reported profitability — but it is still a mechanical recombination of two archived components.

Pairing the highest-alpha profitability leg with the highest-alpha conditioner is a sensible completion of the factorial, though it is the most predictable of the recombinations and both parents already sit at the ~4.2% alpha ceiling, so a genuine breakout is unlikely.

This is the only proposal that changes the economic mechanism rather than the parameterization — an interaction between second-moment earnings risk and callable claims — and it is a clean discriminating test of risk-compensation versus mispricing, though the standalone earnings-volatility leg overlaps a published anomaly and a 3-observation annual VOL is statistically noisy.

This is a mechanical splice of three archive signals — QualityIndexProfit with the profitability leg swapped for the already-tested R&D-restored version — with no new economic content beyond what IntangibleProfitConservatism and IntangibleProfitRollover jointly established, so it is effectively a rediscovery/cosmetic recombination rather than a new hypothesis.

Beyond being a four-component kitchen-sink of already-tested legs (dp intensity, dlc/lt from ShortDebtShareProfit, act/lct from IntangibleProfitWithSlack), the nested SUMRANK silently weights conservatism at 50% and each funding component at 25%, which contradicts the stated "three separable aspects" framing and makes any result uninterpretable as a test of dimensionality.

The floor-vs-level question is a legitimate persistence test, but it is asked here by stacking three previously validated components at once (TS_MIN from ProfitFloorConservatism, R&D restoration, and the two-part quality index), so a change in alpha cannot be attributed to the floor construction — the clean version would vary only TS_MIN against an existing archive baseline.

This is the only proposal that fixes a real measurement asymmetry rather than reshuffling legs — capitalizing the R&D stock in the denominator directly tests whether the intangible premium is productivity or a mechanical numerator inflation — though the construction is internally half-consistent (full current-year spend is added back with no amortization charge against the capitalized stock) and the R&D-capitalization idea itself is well-trodden in the literature.

Filling the {stability}×{conservatism} cell of the 2×2 is a defensible isolated design test given FragileEarningsRollover worked, but note it discards the profitability level entirely, so a positive result may simply reload the well-known low-earnings-volatility quality anomaly interacted with an asset-age/capital-intensity proxy, and the hypothesis text sloppily calls high dp intensity "aggressive depreciation" where the rest of the archive calls it conservative.

This is explicitly the same economic content as proposal 1 with only the aggregation operator changed — a textbook cosmetic variant, and one whose rank-product form is already the dominant construction throughout the archive, so it adds no information the existing pairwise multiplicative signals have not already provided.

This is structurally identical to the archived QualityIndexProfit with both legs swapped for their already-tested upgraded versions, so it is a recombination of known components rather than a new mechanism, and SUMRANK-averaging a strong conservatism leg with a rollover leg whose standalone alpha (4.8%) already exceeds the index's is more likely to dilute than to add.

This is a legitimate internal-consistency repair — MA(xrd,5) is exactly the straight-line amortization matching a five-year TS_SUM stock, so numerator and denominator now use the same capitalization convention — and it is genuinely diagnostic, since for steady-state R&D spenders the numerator collapses back toward reported EBIT and thus cleanly isolates whether the intangible premium is an addback artifact.

The hypothesis claims both gross-basis corrections are applied to the profitability ratio, but the expression's denominator (at + R&D stock) never restores accumulated depreciation, so the stated "consistent definition of invested capital" is not what the expression computes; it is also a two-component swap on the already-tested AgeAdjustedProfitConservatism/PolicyRate pair.

This is FloorRestoredProfitConservatism (fmb 6.30, Sharpe 0.461) with the net-base depreciation rate swapped for the gross-base version already tested in PolicyRateConservatismProfit — a single-component substitution whose likely outcome is a small interpolation between two known results, i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a new economic test.

The pairing of tax-expense validation with a gross-base depreciation policy rate is a coherent and previously untested cell with a real economic tension (heavy book depreciation should suppress book-tax conformity), but tax/assets is close to a rescaled pretax profitability measure and edges toward the known book-tax-difference / tax-expense-surprise literature, so its incremental content is uncertain.

Stability of the depreciation rate is a genuinely different construct from its level or direction and is a useful interpretive discriminator, though the reviewer should note that VOL over only three annual observations of an age-contaminated net-base ratio will mechanically penalize firms with trending (aging or acquisitive) asset bases, and prior volatility-conditioner cells in this archive have produced weak or negative alphas.
